Customer-initiated early settlement of one installment or payoff of every remaining installment
Payment-method recovery: when the plan carries no stored PM, list the Stripe customer's cards and backfill the winner onto the plan
Installments are flipped to 'processing' before the charge and reverted to 'scheduled' with last_failure_reason when Stripe declines
The payment is applied to the rental charge ledger INLINE — a Payment entry, a reduction of the oldest open Rental charge and a payment_applications row — with no HTTP hop to apply-payment
A single PaymentIntent covering all remaining installments marks every slot paid and the plan completed
installment_plans.stripe_customer_id is backfilled from the customer row whenever the plan is missing it
Charges go to the tenant's current charge platform account and the choice is stamped on payments.platform_account
Place a security-deposit authorisation on the renter's saved card as a manual-capture PaymentIntent (authorize only, never charge)
Ask Stripe whether the recorded hold is still alive before refusing — a DB 'held' is not proof of a live authorisation
Only canceled / succeeded / requires_payment_method conclusively mean the authorisation is dead; anything still in motion is treated as alive so a card is never authorised twice
The dead-status map is duplicated in create-hold-checkout because _shared/stripe-client.ts is owned by another workstream and this guard pair had to ship without touching it

GMT incident, Aug 2026: rentals.deposit_hold_status is written once and never revisited, so an expired authorisation still reads 'held' and every placement path short-circuits — 'I cannot refresh the hold'
Configured authorisation for the widest caller set of the deposit family: service-role webhooks, portal staff, the signed-in renter, and unidentified guest-booking automation

Guest bookings are admitted with no session at all for AUTOMATIC placement only — the webhook path needs metadata only the portal sets, so refusing would silently stop deposits on every customer-originated booking
A proven human identity always wins over a client-supplied actor when writing the deposit_hold_links ledger, so nobody can sign another person's name to a card authorisation
Two-tier extension guard: auto-extend rentals never get a hold from any caller; manually-extended rentals are blocked only for AUTOMATIC callers, and deliberate staff action passes manualOverride
A stale 'held' row is corrected to the truth before the claim, anchored to the exact status AND PaymentIntent probed, because the refresh cron can swap in a brand-new live PI under the same status
Yield to rows owned by another worker ('processing') or by the refresh cron ('refreshing') so the claim can never take a slot mid-flight and duplicate the authorisation
A numeric per-rental deposit override always wins, INCLUDING an explicit 0 meaning the operator opted out; only NULL falls back to the tenant default
per_vehicle deposit mode reads vehicles.security_deposit, hard-scoped to GMT's tenant id because the other per_vehicle tenants have a $0 global and would start collecting holds they do not take today
deposit_source and the full estimate_inputs are recorded on the ledger row so 'why was THIS amount authorised?' is answerable months later
Atomic compare-and-set claim of the hold slot which also MINTS deposit_hold_attempt_seq — only one caller can win, so only one caller can mint the attempt number
The Stripe idempotency key is keyed on the ATTEMPT, not the rental and not the dead PaymentIntent — both earlier schemes replayed a cached decline into a fresh attempt
Releasing the 'processing' claim is the recovery-critical write of every failure path: it runs first, retries once, and can never throw
The deposit_hold_links row is written BEFORE Stripe is contacted, so a crashed or timed-out attempt still leaves a discoverable trace of a possible orphan authorisation
supabase-js RESOLVES with {error} on a Postgres error but REJECTS on a transport failure, so both must be caught around every bookkeeping and claim write
Card-feature downgrade ladder (extended authorization + multicapture down to nothing) because unapproved Connect accounts error instead of silently ignoring the request
The real expiry is read from the charge's capture_before with its provenance persisted — never a hardcoded 31 days, which is what let holds die silently while the DB still showed 'held'
deposit_hold_chain_expires_at is a cache and a placement-only floor, not the authority: the refresher recomputes the bound from the rental's LIVE end_date on every pass
The success write is a compare-and-set on 'processing' AND our own attempt_seq; zero rows updated means we no longer own the slot and our authorisation is the orphan
A transport rejection on the success write is ambiguous, so the row is re-read before treating a live authorisation as an orphan and cancelling it
When the record write fails AND the cancel fails, a live authorisation exists that no row points at — the ledger row is then its only trace and is written either way
deposit_hold_target_amount is deliberately left NULL: two amount columns with no defined precedence will drift on a money path, so it is wired up together with its reader or not at all
Connect account, Stripe mode and currency of the hold are anchored on the rental so refresh/capture/release survive a UK->UAE platform flip mid-rental
Card brand/last4/expiry/funding are captured off the PaymentMethod so a 90-day chain is auditable and debit stacking is detectable without a Stripe round-trip per rental
Per-rental integration-readiness verdict emailed to the super admin on EVERY rental creation across all tenants
Fired by the AFTER INSERT trigger on public.rentals through pg_net, so the caller is the database itself and carries no user JWT
verify_jwt = false; the internal caller proves itself with x-platform-secret validated by the service-role-only platform_verify_secret() RPC
The email is rendered from rentals.creation_context — a FROZEN snapshot of Stripe / BoldSign / Bonzah / subscription readiness at the moment the rental was created — plus rentals.health_severity
Three-level triage (ok / warning / critical) drives subject line, colour and the 'why this needs your eyes' reason list
AI identity verification orchestrator: OCR the document, face-match it against the selfie, then write one verdict onto the verification record
Face-match outcome maps to the tri-state verdict: isMatch -> verified/GREEN, needsReview -> review_required/RETRY, otherwise rejected/RED
Additional-driver sessions carry customer_id = NULL and external_user_id 'additional_driver_<uuid>', so the verdict is routed onto rental_additional_drivers instead of customers
A per-tenant blocked_identities hit overrides a GREEN verdict, rejects the verification and blocks the customer row
qr_session_token is nulled on completion so a finished mobile-handoff link cannot be replayed
OCR output backfills the customer's license_number and date_of_birth alongside identity_verification_status
OCR or face-match failure completes the record as RED with a rejection_reason and still answers HTTP 200, so the caller renders a verdict rather than an error
Sessions are looked up by identity_verifications.session_id, not by id — the row id is captured once and reused for every subsequent update
Twilio recordingStatusCallback pipeline: download the MP3, transcribe with Whisper, summarise with GPT, and store transcript + summary + action items on the call log
The recording is re-hosted in the 'voicemails' storage bucket so the browser can play it without Twilio Basic auth
The MP3 is fetched with the TENANT's own Twilio account SID/auth token, falling back to an unauthenticated request
Whisper is billed per MINUTE, not per token, so usage is logged with an explicit costOverride of duration/60 * $0.006
The matching voice chat message gets metadata.has_transcript so the chat UI can offer the transcript without re-querying call_logs
Every degraded path still answers HTTP 200 so Twilio does not retry: a failed download saves the raw Twilio URL, a failed transcription saves '[Transcription failed]'
Hourly off-session collection cron for installment plans in collection_mode='auto' with any open past-due invoice
Every open past-due installment on a plan is summed into ONE PaymentIntent and settled against the LATEST slot, which cascades supersession over the earlier ones (PAYG-style)
A 24h cooldown on installment_plans.last_reminder_sent_at throttles both the charge attempt and the reminder to one per day
Three consecutive authentication_required failures flip the plan to manual collection; any non-SCA failure resets the counter

installment_plans has no platform_account column, so the saved card is charged on the platform of the EARLIEST Stripe payment on the rental — charging with the tenant's current model after a UK->UAE flip throws 'No such customer'
A plan in auto mode with no saved card is flipped to manual and logged rather than retried forever
Optional only_rental_id body scoping hard-restricts a manual dispatch to one rental's plans so it can never charge another tenant
Every auto-charge outcome is written to installment_notifications as an operator-visible audit event
Polls Stripe for a Pending checkout session and commits the payment locally — the fallback used when the Stripe webhook never lands (and in dev, never fires)
Even an ALREADY-settled payment re-runs the installment lookup-and-settle, so revisiting the success page retroactively settles a slot left 'open' by an older code path

A category-targeted payment that does not include 'Rental' must never settle an installment slot — settling a Tax payment against a slot is the root cause of 'Tax: Not Paid but Collected = Tax amount' on installment rentals

The payments UPDATE error is now checked: it used to fail silently (missing paid_at column, chk_pnl_category_valid rejecting Extension* categories, FIFO ignoring target_categories) and the UI showed 'Payment Received' on a row still Pending
A payment carrying extension_id finalises its rental extension atomically through the RPC, which extends end_date without ever shrinking it and is idempotent
The alreadyProcessed branch returns rentalId so the booking-success safety net can still call place-deposit-hold when the webhook beat it to the row (R-b631e8 reproducer)
Settling the slot also activates the plan and captures the saved payment method, choosing collection_mode auto or manual from whether a PM was recoverable
Installment settlement uses DB signals only — no Stripe metadata — so it works regardless of what create-checkout-session stamped
Legacy fallback for pre-Phase-3 payments with no extension_id: clear rentals.extension_checkout_url / extension_amount from target_categories
Per-category refund engine (Rental / Tax / Service Fee / Security Deposit / Extension*) that validates against the ledger before touching Stripe
Refundable amount is derived from the ledger: total charged minus remaining equals paid, minus refunds already recorded for that category
Stripe is the authority on how much is still refundable on a PaymentIntent — the local payments.refund_amount drifts when manual refunds, mixed payments or earlier failures leave it stale
When the request exceeds what Stripe still allows, refund what Stripe allows and record the remainder as a manual (ledger-only) refund with an explicit reconciliation note

An Extension-category refund is refused without an extensionId, because an unscoped one produces orphaned ledger rows and an un-updated payment status — a stale client bundle is the usual cause, so it fails loudly
The Stripe payment to refund is found through payment_applications on THIS category's charges, not by taking the most recent Stripe payment on the rental (which could be an unrelated deposit capture)
The payment already synced by the Stripe block keeps its synced refund_amount; re-adding its share here is the $1.22-charge-becomes-$2.44-refund bug
The refund is allocated across every payment that contributed to the category's charges, most-applied-first, flipping each to Refunded or Partial Refund
capture_status is never touched by a refund — its CHECK constraint only allows requires_capture/captured/cancelled/expired; refund state lives on status + refund_amount + refund_processed_at
The unique index (rental_id, due_date, type, category, extension_id) makes two same-day refunds on one category collide, so the second MERGES into the existing Refund row instead of inserting
A PaymentIntent still at requires_capture cannot be refunded — the operator is told to capture first
Charge-due reminder cadence: Upcoming at T-2 days, Due on the day, then Overdue1..5 at exactly 1, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days past due
With respect_credit_coverage on, a charge already covered by the customer's balance raises no reminder
Every stage is individually switchable through the reminder_settings key/value table, with max_overdue_reminders capping the overdue ladder
Duplicate-key errors on reminder_events are swallowed: the unique constraint IS the idempotency mechanism for a job that may run more than once a day
This job only RECORDS reminder_events — the preview text says the customer will be notified 'once channels are connected', so no email/SMS leaves the system here
One endpoint, two modes: a body with paymentId performs an immediate single refund, an empty body runs the scheduled batch of refunds due today
The refunded amount is split across Rental / Tax / Service Fee / Security Deposit in proportion to the latest invoice's breakdown and posted as one Refund ledger row per category
payments.refund_status walks processing -> completed or failed, with the Stripe error appended to refund_reason on failure
The batch answers HTTP 200 with success:false on a fatal error, deliberately, so the supabase-js caller does not raise FunctionsHttpError
Each refund is created with the keys and connected account of the platform the payment was CREATED on (payments.platform_account), never the tenant's current model
One-shot full RAG index build: every indexed table, for every active tenant, embedded and upserted into rag_documents
knowledge_articles are indexed with BOTH the tenant's own rows and the global rows (tenant_id IS NULL), unlike every other table which is strictly tenant-scoped
Document loaders take the tenant's currency_code, so embedded text renders money in the tenant's own currency rather than a hardcoded $
rag_documents is keyed on (tenant_id, source_table, source_id), which makes a re-run an update rather than a duplicate
Conversion, embedding and upsert failures are counted per table and never abort the run — a partial index is better than none
Incremental RAG maintenance: drain rag_sync_queue (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE) into rag_documents, capped per invocation
PGRST116 on the source row means it was deleted after the queue trigger fired, so the item is treated as a DELETE rather than an error
A failed queue item is still stamped processed_at (with error_message) so one poison row can never stall the whole queue
Tenant currency codes are cached per run so a queue full of one tenant's rows costs one tenants lookup
The document-load, embed and upsert block is duplicated byte-for-byte from rag-init; the two must be changed together
Six-hourly sweep that reconciles every non-terminal deposit hold in the database against the truth at Stripe

Nothing else in the codebase ever reads Stripe back for a hold: webhooks look PaymentIntents up by payments.stripe_payment_intent_id, but a hold's id lives on rentals.deposit_hold_payment_intent_id and has no payments row at all

PRINCIPLE 1 — record-anchored: the hold is read with the account, mode and platform it was CREATED under, never the tenant's current values, because wrong-platform keys make Stripe report the PI as missing, which looks exactly like an expired hold

PRINCIPLE 2 — fail safe, never open: anything inconclusive leaves the row exactly as it is; no state that would allow a second authorisation is ever written on a guess, and no authorisation is cancelled without proving it is an orphan

A row saying 'held' is never demoted on an inconclusive read: place-deposit-hold, create-hold-checkout, cancel-rental-refund, deduct-from-deposit and sync-deposit-hold all key on the literal 'held', so demoting would unblock a second authorisation AND stop the release path at once

PRINCIPLE 3 — expiry provenance: deposit_hold_expires_at is only ever written from a real capture_before, because resolveHoldExpiry's now+7d fallback MOVES on every call and would re-arm the clock so a reconciled rental could never enter the refresh window

EC-23: never insert a payments row, not even for a hold Stripe reports as captured — backfilling payments keyed on a deposit-hold PaymentIntent arms the rental-cancellation path on every rental it touches

Compare-and-set on BOTH the status read AND the PaymentIntent probed: the refresh engine can cancel PI_A and install a live PI_B under the same 'held' status, so a status-only CAS would stamp 'expired' over a live authorisation

The only reaper of rows stranded in a claim state (processing / refreshing / capturing) by a crash, a timeout or a mid-flight deploy — 30 minutes stale, with a recent deposit_hold_links row as the stronger liveness signal

Orphan sweep A: a deposit_hold_links row still 'pending' an hour later belongs to a writer that died — if its PaymentIntent is live and is not the rental's current hold, it is a renter's money held twice

Orphan sweep B: superseded PaymentIntents still at requires_capture, keyset-paginated oldest-first over the whole lookback with ledger markers, because a DESC limit(40) query re-reads the newest page forever and the orphans that matter are the OLD ones
The 35-day superseded lookback is a network fact, not an optimistic assumption: no card authorisation outlives 30 days on any network (Visa 29d18h)

loadRental / loadTenant THROW instead of returning undefined: a silently-undefined rental would make the 'is this the current hold?' comparison false and cancel a live 90-day authorisation on the strength of a database that did not answer

A cancelled PaymentIntent is not always a network expiry: cancellation_reason 'requested_by_customer' or deposit_hold_release_requested_at means a human asked, so the row records 'released' rather than a silent 'expired'
verify_jwt=false, so the only gate is in this file: either the pg_cron x-platform-secret validated by platform_verify_secret(), or a super-admin user JWT resolved through app_users

The service-role bearer is deliberately NOT accepted: a valid production service_role JWT is committed in plaintext at supabase/migrations/20260520170000_schedule_tesla_sync_cron.sql and is pending rotation

Deploy order matters: net.http_post is asynchronous, so a 401 lands in net._http_response and never in cron.job_run_details — a cron sending the wrong credential looks perfectly healthy while nothing is reconciled
A cron_runs heartbeat row per invocation, with scoped and dry runs recorded under a DIFFERENT job_name so they cannot satisfy a dead-man alert on the real 6-hourly schedule
Keyset pagination, never offset: this pass writes terminal statuses that REMOVE rows from the very filter it is paging over, so each offset page would skip exactly as many rows as it corrected
Each sweep gets its own wall-clock reserve on top of the main deadline, because they used to share one and whichever ran second was starved on every busy run

A hold Stripe reports as requires_payment_method is handed back to the placement engine with a retry time but deliberately WITHOUT bumping deposit_hold_failure_count — a reconciler seeing the same failure four times a day would compound the backoff into silence

closeLink returns whether the write actually landed: supabase-js resolves on a failed statement, so an unchecked update followed by linksResolved++ is bookkeeping that lies in the direction of 'nothing to see here'

cron_runs.total_due is counted separately from what is processed so truncation is a visible, alertable signal rather than silent (EC-20); it is never inferred from examined < totalDue, which would cry wolf on a healthy pass

Safety net for the invite-registration flow: a renter who passes verification (GREEN) but never clicks 'Complete Registration' leaves a verification with customer_id NULL and no customer row, so the operator never sees them
Flow Auto Rentals' 'Mary J Davis' had to be added by hand — the incident this job exists to prevent

MIN_AGE is 8 days, deliberately BEYOND the 7-day invite TTL, so a customer is only materialised once the renter's invite has expired — otherwise submit-customer-registration would hit our row, error 'email already exists' and permanently block the renter
customers.email is unique PER TENANT, so the dedup match must be tenant-scoped, case-INSENSITIVE, and must escape LIKE metacharacters so john_doe@x.com is matched literally
The global blacklist, blocked-email and blocked-document guards are mirrored from submit-customer-registration so a blocked identity is never materialised by the back door
Deliberately side-effect free: it creates data only and sends no email, SMS or webhook; phone is form-only so it is left NULL for the operator to complete

Re-runs are safe: an existing same-tenant customer causes the orphaned verification to be BACK-LINKED rather than duplicated, and the window is clamped so a large maxAgeDays cannot defeat the flood guard
Platform-subscription reconciliation: Stripe is the authority, the DB is a cache, and this pass repairs the cache across all four account/mode cells

Webhooks silently froze the DB in production: handleSubscriptionUpdated threw RangeError on every subscription.updated once Stripe moved current_period_* onto items in API 2025-03-31, and the status CHECK rejected 'incomplete_expired', which can make Stripe auto-disable the endpoint
SAFETY INVARIANT 1 — dry run by default: {"dryRun": false} must be passed explicitly before anything is written

SAFETY INVARIANT 2 — never auto go-live: the webhook flips tenants.stripe_mode and bonzah_mode to live, so replaying historic subscriptions through that path would charge real customers and bind real insurance policies; this function writes ONLY to tenant_subscriptions
SAFETY INVARIANT 3 — no invented rows: a Stripe subscription that cannot be resolved to a tenant is reported as an orphan, never guessed at

The headline price is the LARGEST licensed (non-metered) item amount times quantity — items.data[0] is a coin flip because these subscriptions carry a metered e-sign line and a $1 card-verification line, and reading [0] once rewrote a $350/mo plan as $1/mo

The card is looked up beyond subscription.default_payment_method (customer invoice_settings, paymentMethods.list, legacy default_source, then the latest invoice's charge) — reading only the former left 19 of 26 live subscriptions showing 'No payment method on file'
Several of the longest-standing paying tenants bill through a legacy customer default_source Card object, which paymentMethods.list never returns

Invoice reconciliation is the gap that permanently locks out a paying customer: the portal's 7-day grace clock is anchored on the oldest LOCAL open invoice, so a lost invoice.paid leaves the tenant paywalled and pointed at an invoice Stripe already considers settled

stripe_invoice_pdf and hosted_invoice_url are excluded from drift comparison because Stripe rotates their token — a first production dry run reported 29 of 29 invoices as drifted, all URL-only — and they are FILLED when missing, never rewritten

attempt_count is the only thing separating a DECLINED invoice from one merely not due yet (Stripe leaves both at status='open'), and it drives the admin dashboard's red 'Payment failed' vs amber 'Unpaid' badge

Every compared column must appear in the select: one missing reads back undefined, never equals Stripe, and reports the row as drifted forever — 59 permanently 'changed' invoices would bury the one real change

The subscription row is adopted BEFORE its invoices, because invoices link by tenant_subscriptions.id and nothing backfills a NULL — an unlinked invoice is discarded by the portal, so a past_due tenant got neither a warning nor a pay link
Invoices are reconciled before the 'subscription already in sync -> continue' short-circuit, because a perfectly in-sync subscription can still own the stale invoice the paywall actually decides on

A tenant migrated to the UAE account keeps a winding-down UK subscription that Stripe still reports as active; writing it back would trip idx_tenant_subscriptions_active or make the retired UK row masquerade as current

Never blank a stored value: a zero/unresolvable amount, a null card and a null billing period are all omitted from the payload rather than written, because an ordinary hourly run once wiped card details the webhook had captured at checkout

This function had no authorisation check at all — Supabase's default verify_jwt accepts the PUBLIC anon key shipped in every browser bundle, and the response body is a cross-tenant dump of every tenant's subscription, customer ids and amounts
Two legitimate callers: the hourly pg_cron job presenting the service-role key, and a super admin pressing 'Sync now', verified through app_users.is_super_admin and is_active
All four cells (uk/uae x live/test) are walked and a missing key is reported explicitly — a silently skipped account is exactly how drift hides

Stripe subscriptions outlive tenants, so a metadata tenant_id is existence-checked before any write: an FK insert would simply error, and the row is reported as an orphan for a human to cancel in Stripe

amount_refunded is deliberately NOT compared: Stripe reports refunds on the CHARGE, so sourcing it would cost 300+ API calls an hour and comparing an unreadable field would report permanent phantom drift; the charge.refunded webhook owns it
Record what the operator actually paid the issuing authority for a traffic fine, separate from what is recharged to the customer
Every authority payment posts a matching P&L Cost entry in the Fines category, linked back to the fine through source_ref
The P&L entry carries a unique reference of the form 'authority:<payment id>', so a duplicate key means the cost was already booked and is logged rather than treated as a failure
A failed P&L insert never fails the request — the authority payment itself is the record of truth and the accounting entry is repaired separately
Per-minute cron safety net: scan recent Pending Stripe payments, retrieve each session, and commit anything that actually paid

Root cause it covers: a Stripe webhook routed to the wrong test/live URL fails signature verification with a 400, leaving the booking-success page's client-side chain as the only commit path — so a stale or down app strands the payment as Pending forever

Committing the payment is enough: auto_fifo_on_payment_completed fires on the status transition, runs payment_apply_fifo_v2 to drain the ledger, and auto_settle_payg_on_ledger_drain flips the matching PAYG accrual to paid

Second pass heals CAPTURED payments stranded as status='Credit' with $0 allocated on a rental that still owes — real Stripe money that FIFO refused to allocate to Extension* charges (globalmotiontransport R-63b168, 'Stripe payment not recording on the website')

The heal only runs when the rental genuinely still has open charge balance, so a legitimate overpayment credit is never disturbed, and the payment is only counted healed once it actually moves off 'Credit'
Stripe client and connected account are resolved PER PAYMENT from payments.platform_account, not the tenant's current payment model
Keep a security-deposit authorisation alive across a long rental by CHAINING it: cancel before expiry and place a replacement on the saved card, 4-18 links for a 90-120 day rental
This file is only the DRIVER — which rentals are due, in what order, how many per run, and the heartbeat; every per-rental decision lives in _shared/deposit-hold-refresh.ts
The engine was extracted because refresh-deposit-holds and sandbox-refresh-deposit-holds were hand-maintained verbatim forks, so the Time Machine was green-lighting logic production no longer ran

Ordered (oldest deadline first, unknown expiry ahead of everything) and limited with a wall-clock budget: the old serial unbounded loop was killed by the 400s ceiling, stranding rows in 'refreshing' that nothing reaps
A .lt() comparison against a NULL deposit_hold_expires_at yields NULL, not true, so rows with no known expiry were invisible to the old due filter

'failed' rows are retried once backoff elapses, but ONLY those evidencing a real prior authorization (a PaymentIntent or a placed-at stamp) — the Stripe webhooks write the same 'failed' when a FIRST placement never succeeded and those are not this engine's to touch
Rental lifecycle gating is a terminal-status DENY list rather than an ('Active','Pending') allow list, so a status nobody enumerated cannot silently end a chain

config_unavailable is kept OUT of the failure count — one mis-configured tenant reporting failures forever trains whoever watches cron_runs to ignore the dead-man signal — but raises one aggregated, day-deduped bell per tenant instead

Rows parked in 'refreshing' by a killed run are COUNTED but never reaped here: deciding whether such a row's authorization exists requires probing Stripe, which belongs to the reconciler, and guessing is how a renter ends up with two live holds

An engine that throws breaks its own return-don't-throw contract, so nothing inside it can have written a status; the driver raises an alert with moneyState 'unknown' and the attempt_seq the engine would have claimed, so a partially-raised alert dedupes

verify_jwt=false plus a caller-supplied only_rental_id on a DESTRUCTIVE path (it cancels the live authorisation before replacing it) — so the gate accepts only the pg_cron platform secret or a super-admin user JWT
A cron_runs row is opened before any work and closed with total_due / processed / succeeded / failed / truncated, so 'no alerts' can be told apart from 'the job is dead'
Before these alerts, a chain that died on day 45 of a 90-day rental was discovered when the car came back
Refund an entire installment plan: every paid installment plus the upfront payment, then cancel the plan and its remaining scheduled slots
resolveForRecord anchors the Stripe client and connected account on the linked PAYMENT's platform_account, never the tenant's current model, which may have flipped since the charge was made

Per-category refund ledger rows are derived from payment_applications joined to the charges they paid, falling back to the invoice breakdown (deposit, service fee, tax, delivery) and finally to a single Rental row
A Stripe charge_already_refunded error still counts toward totalRefunded — the money is back either way and the run must not report a false failure
Installments marked paid by hand carry no PaymentIntent, so there is nothing to refund at Stripe and only the ledger and plan state change
Fatal errors are returned as HTTP 200 with success:false, so the portal caller renders the partial result instead of a transport error
Reject a booking end to end: release or refund every active payment, add Refund ledger rows, delete the P&L revenue, cancel the rental, release the vehicle and cancel unpaid charges
A payment still at requires_capture is RELEASED by cancelling the PaymentIntent; a captured one is refunded — and an 'already cancelled/expired' Stripe error is treated as a successful release
A payment with an amount but no Stripe PaymentIntent is flagged refund_status='pending_manual' for a human to settle, rather than silently marked refunded
A missing stripe_payment_intent_id is resolved from the checkout session and persisted back onto the payment row for future operations
payment_applications, payment ledger entries and charge remaining_amounts are deliberately kept intact so the UI still shows what was paid; Refund rows are ADDED per category instead
P&L revenue entries are removed with a LIKE match on source_ref prefixed by the payment id, which is the only link between a payment and its revenue rows
Each payment is cancelled or refunded on the platform account it was CREATED on, resolved per record rather than from the tenant's current model
Rejection releases the vehicle back to Available, which is what makes the slot bookable again

Record-anchored Stripe resolution: every money operation uses the platform account, connected account and mode the RECORD was created under, never the tenant's current payment_model — the invariant that survives the UK->UAE migration

Repo-wide operating assumption: a Stripe webhook is a delivery guarantee, not a consistency guarantee — every money surface therefore carries a poll, a self-heal or a reconciler that reads Stripe back

cron_runs dead-man heartbeat convention: open a row before any work, close it with total_due/processed/succeeded/failed/truncated, and give scoped or dry runs a different job_name so they cannot satisfy the alert for the real schedule

Installment settlement convention: pick the LATEST open slot due today or earlier and call installment_settle_invoice, which cumulatively supersedes the earlier open slots (PAYG-style) — reimplemented identically in the cron, the poll fallback and the webhooks

Category-refund ledger convention: a refund is always posted as one negative Refund ledger row per category with remaining_amount 0, sourced from payment_applications where possible and from the invoice breakdown otherwise

hyperedges.label: The repair layer that exists because webhooks drop
